comparisons.peer_summary: Liquidity in nonbank entities, including the Parent, NB Holdings, and other regulated entities like broker-dealers, is held primarily as cash deposited at BANA and high-quality, liquid, unencumbered securities. Transfers from these entities to the Parent or other subsidiaries may require prior regulatory approval due to regulatory restrictions and minimum requirements, and other regulated entities also hold unencumbered investment-grade securities and equities that may generate additional liquidity.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC disclose the structure of liquidity and capital support provided to regulated subsidiaries, particularly broker-dealers. GS explicitly details substantial equity, subordinated indebtedness, and loans provided by the holding company to its regulated subsidiaries (e.g., $38.69 billion in equity/sub-debt to GS&Co.). Similarly, BAC notes that liquidity held in nonbank entities, primarily broker-dealer subsidiaries, exists but highlights that transfers of this liquidity to the parent or other subsidiaries may require prior regulatory approval due to regulatory restrictions. Both disclosures address the interplay between subsidiary funding/liquidity and regulatory constraints on moving capital up the chain.

sentences.text: Group Inc. has provided substantial amounts of equity and subordinated indebtedness, directly or indirectly, to its regulated subsidiaries.

Group Inc. also provides financing, directly or indirectly, in the form of: $131.82 billion of unsubordinated loans (including secured loans of $59.97 billion) and $32.92 billion of collateral and cash deposits to these entities as of December 2024.
Liquidity is also held in nonbank entities, including the Parent, NB Holdings and other regulated entities.

Liquidity held in other regulated entities, comprised primarily of broker-dealer subsidiaries, is primarily available to meet the obligations of that entity, and transfers to the Parent or to any other subsidiary may be subject to prior regulatory approval due to regulatory restrictions and minimum requirements.

comparisons.peer_summary: Non-bank long-term debt includes debt issued by the parent holding company, consolidated non-bank subsidiaries (such as broker-dealers), and consolidated hedging activities, totaling $87.8 billion as of December 31, 2024. Local country and other debt comprises debt issued by affiliates to support local operations, including certain secured financing within the non-bank category.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citi provide details on the financial structure of their non-bank subsidiaries, specifically broker-dealers. GS quantifies the equity and subordinated indebtedness invested in its regulated subsidiaries, such as $38.69 billion in GS&Co. (a broker-dealer). Citi’s disclosure defines 'non-bank' long-term debt to include debt issued by the parent holding company and non-bank subsidiaries like broker-dealers, noting that $87.8 billion of long-term debt was issued by Citi's broker-dealer and other subsidiaries as of December 31, 2024. Both filings highlight the significant capital and debt obligations associated with their broker-dealer subsidiaries.

sentences.text: For example, as of December 2024, Group Inc. had $38.69 billion of equity and subordinated indebtedness invested in GS&Co., its principal U.S. registered broker-dealer; $47.21 billion invested in GSI, a regulated U.K. broker-dealer; $2.08 billion invested in GSJCL, a regulated Japanese broker-dealer; $62.81 billion invested in GS Bank USA, a regulated New York State-chartered bank; and $5.30 billion invested in GSIB, a regulated U.K. bank.

(1) Non-bank includes long-term debt issued to third parties by the parent holding company (Citigroup) and Citi's non-bank subsidiaries (including broker-dealer subsidiaries) that are consolidated into Citigroup.
As of December 31, 2024, non-bank included $87.8 billion of long-term debt issued by Citi's broker-dealer and other subsidiaries that are consolidated into Citigroup.
